artifact.canonical_name: AoiZora: Topology-Aware Auto-Parallel Optimization for Inference of Diffusion Transformers

claims.text: The authors propose AoiZora, a topology-aware auto-parallel optimizer for distributed video-diffusion inference.

limitations: The evidence is the authors' arXiv paper/model card and reported evaluations; results are not independently reproduced in this Evidence review.
overrides.why_this_special: This June paper is technically valid but is retained as supporting/Paper Watch material unless Candidate Selection has room.

verify TPU topology assumptions and sear.finding: The paper evaluates a topology-aware auto-parallel search for video diffusion inference and reports experiments on TPU v5e topologies; the optimization searches parallelization choices rather than assuming one fixed partition.

overrides.rationale: Primary-paper evidence is valid but lower priority than stronger June themes.

artifact.canonical_name: SwarmX: Agentic Scheduling for Low-Latency Agentic Systems

claims.text: The authors propose SwarmX, a scheduler designed around multi-call and tool-using agent workloads rather than independent inference requests.

limitations: The evidence is the authors' arXiv paper/model card and reported evaluations; results are not independently reproduced in this Evidence review.

verify production/evaluation workloads.finding: SwarmX targets agentic workloads composed of model calls and tool executions; the paper reports production-scale cluster context and evaluation of scheduling for GPU/CPU resources.

artifact.canonical_name: ShareLock: A Stealthy Multi-Tool Threshold Poisoning Attack Against MCP

claims.text: The authors introduce ShareLock, a threshold-based multi-tool poisoning attack for MCP ecosystems.

limitations: The evidence is the authors' arXiv paper/model card and reported evaluations; results are not independently reproduced in this Evidence review.

verify threat model and MCP assumptions.finding: ShareLock models MCP tool-poisoning across multiple tools, using threshold secret sharing to distribute a hidden instruction and a reconstruction trigger; the threat model assumes multiple tool descriptions can cooperatively contribute to an attack.

artifact.canonical_name: Capability Gates Are Not Authorization: Confused-Deputy Failures in LLM Agent Frameworks

claims.text: The authors distinguish tool capability exposure from per-call authorization and demonstrate confused-deputy risks in common agent frameworks.

limitations: The evidence is the authors' arXiv paper/model card and reported evaluations; results are not independently reproduced in this Evidence review.

verify audited framework versions/defaul.finding: The paper audits pinned public-source versions of LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and Stripe Agent Toolkit, finding default capability gates but no deterministic fail-closed per-call value authorization gate; it evaluates a ScopeGate control.
